ozet: Meccans who turned away from the idols, and Zayd ibn 'Amr; in the years after the Ka'ba was rebuilt, true dreams, solitude and retreat in Hira. The episode ends just before the first revelation.

b10-s01: In the years after the Ka'ba was rebuilt, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) thought more and more about how Allah should be worshipped.
b10-s02: He had seen that worshipping idols brought no good to anyone.
The sources suppose that he thought like the Hanifs, who tried to hold to Abraham's belief in the one God.
b10-s03: Among Quraysh there were others who also questioned the worship of idols.
Every year Quraysh held a festival at one of their idols: they sacrificed to it, stayed beside it, and walked around it.
On one such festival day, four men quietly slipped away from the crowd: Waraqa ibn Nawfal, 'Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh, 'Uthman ibn al-Huwayrith and Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl.
b10-s04: They talked of how their people had strayed from the religion of their father Abraham: they walked around a stone that could neither hear nor see, neither harm nor help.
Each of them had to seek a religion for himself. To find the religion of Abraham, they scattered in different directions.

Waraqa took up Christianity and gained knowledge from the scriptures of the Jews and Christians. 'Uthman went to the Byzantine emperor and became a Christian. 'Ubaydullah remained undecided until he became a Muslim.
b10-s05: Zayd went as far as Syria to find the true religion.

First he spoke with a Jewish scholar, then with a Christian one. Both pointed him to the same religion: the way of the Hanifs, the religion of Abraham. Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian; he worshipped Allah alone.
As Zayd left, he raised his hands and said: «O Allah! I bear witness that I am on the religion of Abraham.»
b10-s06: Zayd became neither a Jew nor a Christian. He left the religion of his people; he kept away from idols, from carrion, from blood, and from animals slaughtered in the name of idols.
To someone who wanted to kill his daughter he would say, «Do not kill her; I will provide for her,» and he would take the child in. «I worship the Lord of Abraham,» he would say.
Asma, the daughter of Abu Bakr, had seen him in his old age, leaning his back against the Ka'ba and saying: «O Quraysh! By Allah, none of you is on the religion of Abraham except me.»
b10-s07: One day before prophethood came, the Prophet met Zayd in the lower part of the valley of Baldah, on the road to Mecca.
A meal was brought before them. Zayd said: «I do not eat what you slaughter on the stones of your idols; I eat only that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned.»
Zayd died before the coming of prophethood.
b10-s08: In Mecca there were some people who, in certain months of the year, withdrew to a secluded place to worship. Quraysh called this tahannuth.
His grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib, too, used to withdraw from time to time to the cave on Hira to worship.
b10-s09: Hira is a mountain rising to the north-east of Mecca.
b10-s10: After he became a prophet, the Messenger of Allah said: «I know a stone in Mecca that used to greet me before I was sent as a prophet; I know it even now.»
b10-s11: As 'A'isha related, revelation began with true dreams seen in sleep; every dream he saw came true just as it was, like the light of morning.
b10-s12: Then solitude was made dear to him.
Every year, when the month of Ramadan came, he would leave the town behind for a month and go up to Hira.
b10-s13: There he would worship for nights on end, without going back to his family.
The sources call this worship tahannuth; the word is explained as turning towards the way of Abraham, the way of the Hanifs.
b10-s14: He would take provisions with him. When they ran out, he would go back to Khadija and take provisions again for as long a time.
b10-s15: During the month he spent at Hira, he fed the poor who came to him.
b10-s16: When the month was over, before going home he would stop at the Ka'ba, walk around it seven times or as often as he wished, and then return home.
b10-s17: From time to time Khadija would also go up to Hira with him.
b10-s18: And one night in Ramadan, he was in Hira again.
